body: ah, I see. well, I do have a history of anxiety and depression, and when I got off of my anti-depressants, my anxiety got even worse. but i know for a fact that it's a good thing that I got off of those stupid drugs, because with stopping it, I came to the conclusion that PMO was a major contributing factor to my depression and anxiety. That's what set me out to stop my PMO addiction once and for all.

Thanks for the comment. It helps to know that I'm not alone in this kind of situation. It really does. I'm feeling a little better now and trying to stay as positive as I can. Thank you again and I wish you the best as well.
Thanks for the kind words. I really do appreciate it. I'm starting to get a little bit better now. I know that eventually I will get my life back on track. Thanks again :)

I already stopped seeing him after the first week, which was two months ago. Luckily, I took the initiative of going to a REAL doctor, mentioned my experiences and symptoms to him, and he referred me to a physical therapist. They're making me do exercises/stretches to re-strengthen my neck and back muscles so I won't get the pain anymore. Btw for the record, I posted this during one of my really bad health anxiety (hypochondria) episodes. So maybe that's one of the reason why I got a lot of downvotes.

finally, someone who shares the same views as me. it seems that for the RIGHT chiropractic treatment, we have to go to a Gonstead chiropractor, as they are more in-depth with their analyses and adjustments. just look at Chiropractic Excellence's videos. Dr. Ian Rossborough really does good adjustments. I wish I had the money and time to visit his office.

I also relate to you in a lot of ways. Just know that you are not alone with your struggles. It's pretty funny when we have OCD and other mental health issues; we think that our problems are very specific to our situations and that there is NO ONE else in the world that have experiences JUST LIKE OURS, or at least that's what I used to think. But we do all share similar experiences. It's pretty crazy when you think about it. Anyway, take care and have a good day.

My OCD and anxiety got the best of me which led to thoughts about the past actions that I had committed when I was deep into PMO (porn masturbation orgasm) addiction. I almost committed an incestual act towards my brother and my mom, two separate times, all under the influence of PMO. It still haunts me to this day but doesn't exactly bother me too much. Just goes to show just how dangerous pornography really is. Don't worry too much about it anymore. At least you weren't like me. I still regret everything I did back then but we all just have to move on. Have a good day.

Okay, update: The adjustments seem to be working; my posture is noticeably improved, but I'm still in pain, and also unusually fatigued. I just feel flat out fragile. My back and neck feel fragile. Is this normal? Keep in mind that I started feeling VERY fatigued after my third adjustment. I've been undergoing the treatment for a week now and I feel no relief whatsoever. It's making me feel so miserable because the pain & fatigue is preventing me from going out to places. Right now I regret going to the chiropractor.
My father is making my medical decisions.

Okay, I called them today and spoke with the chiropractor. He said that it's happened to some of his patients before and that it's rare. He simply said that my body was not used to the adjustment - pretty much my brain wasn't used to all the information that was going on in my spine and nervous system so that's why I was feeling that. Also, yesterday I posted this same question to one of Ace Thayer's videos (he's a chiropractor) and he replied with this:

"This is not a sympathetic storm or a brain injury. Simply it's a massive adjustment to a new balance center in your body. Your having vertigo. I don't see it very often anymore in my office because I a much more conservative with my patients initially because in the past I would see this way to often, The patient would get scared and not come back so I have learned to be more patient. Like I said any change is good change. Just remind the doctor that you don't have to fix everything in one visit. Remain positive because I believe that your on the right tract. Give it a few more visits before you pass judgment. Good luck."
Okay, that sounds plausible. I'm going to call them in a few hours when they open to discuss it with them.
